metadata.title: Projects
metadata.description: Murya (Hausa speech technology), Mapping Voices (open oral-history dataset), the Hausa lexicon, and other projects by Adamu Danjuma Abubakar.

heading: Engineered Systems & Research Platforms
intro: Speech technology, open research datasets, and platforms I have built or lead, with my role in each. My [browser-based research tools](/tools/) are also available to use.
homeIntro: Explore [all projects](/projects/) for more datasets, research, and platforms.

projects.title: Murya
projects.homeSummary: Hear Hausa text read aloud in your browser. Murya pairs offline speech synthesis with a Hausa–English dictionary.
projects.description: Hear Hausa text read aloud or look up a word in the Ƙamus dictionary. Both work offline in the browser after the first download.
highlights: Blind MOS naturalness study running at app.murya.ng/listen; no score is published until each voice has enough ratings
8-speaker Piper VITS model at 22,050 Hz, fine-tuned on the WAXAL Hausa corpus. Weights CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on Hugging Face; application code MIT
Under 110 ms to first audio, running in the browser
Echo suppression so the assistant doesn’t hear its own voice in live conversation

projects.title: Mapping Voices
projects.homeSummary: Explore 221 oral-history collections by place and language. Each record links to the institution that holds the collection.
projects.description: Find oral-history collections by country, language, or theme, then follow each record to the institution that holds it.
highlights: 221 real, publicly documented collections across 120 countries and territories and 125 languages, archived on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22996478)
Zero-dependency static app (Leaflet + OpenStreetMap) with Language Explorer, Theme Explorer, and Coverage Gaps views
Full UI localization in English, Hausa, French, and Arabic with native CLDR pluralization
Open source (MIT code / CC BY 4.0 data) with a public contribution pipeline for institutions and researchers

projects.title: Hausa Lexicon (Ƙamus)
projects.homeSummary: 20,628 Robinson (1914) Hausa–English pairs published on Hugging Face (public domain). Murya’s internal lexicon totals 30,729 entries, adding Wiktionary (CC BY-SA) and an authorized subset of Newman (1977) that is not redistributed.
projects.description: Robinson 1914 Hausa–English lexicon (20,628 pairs, Public Domain) published on Hugging Face, extended internally to 30,729 dictionary-constrained entries with Wiktionary (CC-BY-SA) and a Prof. Paul Newman (1977) research subset kept unpublished per that permission’s terms.
highlights: 20,628 Robinson 1914 pairs published on Hugging Face under public-domain terms
30,729 total entries used for internal lexical grounding (Robinson + Wiktionary + Newman 1977 subset)
Newman (1977) subset is not redistributed

projects.title: Humanities Perspectives on Agentic AI
projects.homeSummary: Why the humanities belong at the centre of agentic-AI governance: contested ideas of agency, four case studies, and a governance framework informed by postcolonial theory.
projects.description: Working paper on why the humanities belong at the centre of agentic-AI governance, drawing on postcolonial theory, cultural pragmatics, and four case studies.
highlights: Grounding conversational AI in Hausa norms of modesty and respect (Kunya & Girmamawa)
Critical analysis of Western anthropocentric agent architectures
A governance framework for autonomous AI agents

projects.title: Global Opportunities
projects.homeSummary: Scholarships, research fellowships, grants, and international jobs in one place, with deadline tracking and email alerts.
projects.description: A global discovery engine and automated deadline tracker for scholarships, research fellowships, international grants, and academic positions worldwide.
highlights: Plain-English opportunity summaries with verified deadline tracking
Automated background web aggregation and listing refresh
Passwordless instant opportunity saving and email match alerts
Built for international researchers, scholars, and fellows

projects.title: Imodoye Writers' Residency
projects.homeSummary: Platform for a writers' residency in Ilorin, Kwara State: fellows, cohorts, and publications, plus blind review for its literary journal, Imodoye Review.
projects.description: Platform for Imodoye, a writers' residency in Ilorin, Kwara State by Dr. Usman Oladipo Akanbi, President of the Association of Nigerian Authors. Seven cohorts in, with its own literary journal, Imodoye Review.
highlights: Content management for fellows, cohorts, partners, and publications
Blind-review editorial workflow feeding submissions to Imodoye Review
Public residency archive and impact reporting, backed by the live database

projects.title: Adab Infrastructure (PropTech)
projects.description: Full-stack property listing and real estate marketplace platform operating across Nigeria with intelligent search portals and verified lister workflows.
highlights: Property search with filters, Google Maps integration, and structured data for SEO
Supabase-backed CMS for listings, inquiries, and services content
Dedicated lister portal, separate from the admin CMS, for verified agent onboarding
